environment.description: Terraform provider runs on an ECS Fargate task within a private subnet (10.200.0.0/24) in vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f. The deployment API is exposed exclusively through a VPC Interface Endpoint (vpce-0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8) for service com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0deadbeef1234abcd with a private DNS entry deploy-api.internal.corp. The VPC has no NAT gateway, no internet gateway, and the subnet route table (rtb-0aabbccdd) contains only local routes (10.200.0.0/16 -> local) and the VPC endpoint ENI route. Security group sg-0x9y8z7w on the Fargate task allows egress only to the VPC endpoint prefix list (pl-0abc123) on port 443. The ECS task role (arn:aws:iam::112233445566:role/terraform-task-restricted) has an IAM permissions boundary (arn:aws:iam::112233445566:policy/NoExternalNetworkBoundary) that denies sts:AssumeRole for any role outside the account and denies ec2:CreateNetworkInterface. The VPC endpoint policy restricts access to only the deployment API actions. Even if command injection occurs via pre_deploy_hook, the injected command cannot exfiltrate data or reach any external service because there is literally no network path out of the VPC — no IGW, no NAT, no VPC peering, no transit gateway attachment. The only reachable endpoint is the internal deployment API via PrivateLink.

config.network: private subnet 10.200.0.0/24, no IGW, no NAT GW, no TGW, no peering, route table rtb-0aabbccdd with only local route
config.vpc_endpoint: vpce-0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8, interface type, private DNS deploy-api.internal.corp
config.security_group_egress: sg-0x9y8z7w allows TCP/443 only to pl-0abc123 (VPC endpoint prefix list)
config.vpc_endpoint_policy: allows only deployment API POST/GET/DELETE on /v1/deployments/*
config.runtime: ECS Fargate, non-root, read-only root filesystem, no ECS Exec enabled
config.dns: VPC DHCP option set with internal DNS only, no external resolution
